implement.summary:
LIQUIDATED DAMAGES CALCULATION — DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED ATTORNEY (not legal advice)

JURISDICTION: The request does not name the governing law of the contract. The calculation below is pure contractual arithmetic (day count × rate, compared with a percentage cap) and does not depend on jurisdiction. No rule of law is relied on for any figure stated. Because the governing jurisdiction is unnamed, no view is expressed on the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause (e.g. penalty-doctrine analysis); that question is outside the four asks. For the avoidance of doubt, if England & Wales law were later confirmed as governing, enforceability would fall to be assessed under Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co Ltd v New Garage & Motor Co Ltd [1915] AC 79 (HL) as restated in Cavendish Square Holding BV v Talal El Makdessi [2015] UKSC 67 — that citation is offered only to flag the open issue, not as a conclusion reached.

FACTS TAKEN AS GIVEN: LD rate £1,250 for each day after 14 March; completion 29 April of the same year; contract price £480,000; cap 10% of the contract price.

FORMULA: LDs payable = min( D × £1,250 , 10% × £480,000 ), where D is the number of delay days.

STEP 1 — DAYS COUNTED (Ask 3): D = 46.
The rate accrues 'for each day after 14 March', so counting begins on 15 March (the day after 14 March) and runs through to the completion date, 29 April, which is included because the works were in delay on that day until completion.
- March: 15–31 March = 31 − 14 = 17 days
- April: 1–29 April = 29 days
- Total: 17 + 29 = 46 days
Cross-check (non-leap year day-of-year): 29 April = day 119; 14 March = day 73; 119 − 73 = 46 days. (A leap year does not affect March–April.)

STEP 2 — UNCAPPED AMOUNT (Ask 4): £57,500.
46 days × £1,250/day = £57,500.
Arithmetic: 46 × 1,000 = 46,000; 46 × 250 = 11,500; 46,000 + 11,500 = 57,500.

STEP 3 — THE CAP: £48,000.
10% × £480,000 = £48,000.

STEP 4 — DOES THE CAP APPLY? (Ask 2): YES.
Uncapped amount £57,500 is greater than the cap of £48,000 (excess = £57,500 − £48,000 = £9,500). The cap is therefore engaged and limits recovery.

STEP 5 — LDs PAYABLE (Ask 1): £48,000.
min(£57,500, £48,000) = £48,000.

ROBUSTNESS OF THE DAY-COUNT CONVENTION: the cap applies under any reasonable convention —
- Counted as above (15 March–29 April inclusive): 46 days → £57,500 → cap applies.
- If 29 April were excluded: 45 days → £56,250 → still above £48,000 → cap applies.
- If 14 March were also included: 47 days → £58,750 → still above £48,000 → cap applies.
The payable figure of £48,000 is therefore unaffected by the convention chosen.

ASSUMPTIONS STATED (corrections would change the inputs but not the method): completion on 29 April is accepted with no extension of time or employer prevention; the cap is 10% of the stated price of £480,000 with no variations; no prior deductions, set-offs or part-payments against LDs; figures in pounds sterling, exclusive of VAT; the LD clause is treated as the operative delay remedy as the request describes it.

ANSWERS: LDs payable £48,000; the cap applies; days counted 46; uncapped amount £57,500; cap £48,000.
